extracted.intended_audience: readers of the Philosophical Transactions — natural philosophers, anatomists, physicians, and instrument-makers
extracted.subtask_description: Short scientific reports and observations including human and animal anatomical case descriptions, a chemical/natural-history treatise on natron/nitre, and design/operation details for a clock movement descended on an inclined plane.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting aged persons
rubrics_metrics.description: Short notice of the names and ages of several very old persons, either living or lately deceased, chiefly in the counties of York and Lincoln.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include individual's name, residence, age, and whether living or died (with year of death when applicable). (Example entries: 'Robert Montgomery, residing in Skipton, aged 126 years.'; 'Mary Allison, of Thorlby, died 1668, aged 108.')

rubrics_metrics.name: Case report of a monstrous child
rubrics_metrics.description: Account of a monstrous child giving date and place (e.g. 'Feb. 29, 1684, at a village called Heisaggar, near Hattersleben') and detailed morphological description of anomalies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record chronology and locality; describe each anomalous structure (left leg excrescence, movable vs fixed pieces, number of toes, loose 'bullet' like appendages, face appearance, excrescences on forehead, hood-like shape behind head, arm knots/joints, tail length with units, mother's age and other children, and immediate outcome — e.g. 'this monster, after it had cried out twice or thrice presently expired'); refer to figures/plates where provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anatomical observation: horny excrescence on ox (hoof/horn formation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Minute description of a preternatural horny excrescence hanging from an ox's neck (where yoke is fastened) and its structure and implications for hoof formation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe structure in detail and relate to broader anatomical theory: 'he thinks, throw great light on the formation and growth of the hoofs of quadrupeds'; compare with similar structures (e.g. spurs of cocks) and connect observations to prior treatises (organ of touch).

rubrics_metrics.name: Anatomical observation: morbid appearances of kidneys
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed account of morbid kidney structure (e.g. cortical part composed of numerous glandular folliculi resembling a bunch of grapes; lack of usual excretory vessels; direct/short communication with pelvis; asymmetry between left and right kidneys; vesicles filled with corrupted blood, urine, gravel, or tartareous matter).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record gross morphology, contents of abnormal glands/vesicles, relative sizes, and infer functional consequences (e.g. urinary secretion prevented from getting into pelvis leading to stagnation and enlargement); compare with analogous glandular disease such as liver acini distension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure for a treatise on nitre (natron)
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizational checklist for discussing 'nitre' (as in the letter: 'In the 1st place... In the 2d... ... In the 11th').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When treating nitre, address in order: 1) whence nitre has its denomination; 2) different names ancient authors ascribe; 3) places whence it comes; 4) description when compositum; 5) number of its principles when chemically resolved; 6) the rise of them; 7) its separation from the water of natron; 8) its use in physic; 9) in agriculture and mechanics; 10) wherein it differs from sal ammoniac; 11) from saltpetre. (Preserve numbered structure when composing such a treatise.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Diagnostic criteria distinguishing natron from saltpetre and sal ammoniac
rubrics_metrics.description: Set of observable/experimental tests and sensory properties to distinguish natron (Egyptian nitre) from saltpetre and from sal ammoniac.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use empirical tests enumerated in the text: fermentation with acids (natron ferments with any acid; saltpetre will not), taste (natron is lixivial), volatile spirit on heating (natron yields a volatile alkali; saltpetre gives a corrosive acid), presence of a red clammy substance in natron, crystallization behavior and crystal form differences, lack of detonation in fire for natron; color and texture differences with sal ammoniac (natron reddish and spongy/perforated vs sal ammoniac not reddish and more compact). Also note reactions when mixed (e.g. trituration with carbonate of soda causes release of ammonia from sal ammoniac).

rubrics_metrics.name: Field/method note: formation and separation of natron crystals
rubrics_metrics.description: Account of natron lakes (Nitria) where natron arises and is condensed by sun-heat into a crystalline film on the lake surface.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document local geography (Nitria, lakes, location relative to Nile/Cairo), note solar evaporation process producing surface film and crystals, and cite field observers (e.g. Dr. Huntington) when describing separation from water of natron.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting uses of natron (medicinal, agricultural, mechanical, dyeing)
rubrics_metrics.description: When reporting on natron, enumerate reputed uses: therapeutic claims (ulcers, inflammations, palsy of tongue, consumptions, colic, hemorrhages, stone), agricultural observations (affecting plant growth/fatness of land), mechanical uses (glass-making), and role in dyeing (making 'true azure').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State ancient authorities (Pliny, Vitruvius) and modern corroboration where available; separate anecdote/ancient claim from experimentally confirmed uses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anatomical description of the uterus (general content requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Full anatomical account of the uterus (cow and human) including outer membrane, arrangement of fleshy/muscular fibres (longitudinal, horizontal, crossed, fasciculi), lymphatic vessels, veins and arteries (networks), nerves, and ducts/vessels peculiar to the uterus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide minute, ordered description following dissection sequence; describe variability (contracted/confused in unimpregnated state; changes during pregnancy); note special vessels' course, size variation, orifices, glandular-like appendices or valves, and relation to surrounding structures (vagina, urethra, os uteri).

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods for revealing uterine structures
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical techniques for detecting uterine vessels/membranes and glandular structures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend careful dissection, maceration of inner membrane in water to make excretory orifices visible (especially in sheep), injection with ink to reveal radicles and capillamenta and to show blood-vessel communication (inject by arteria uteri), use of boiling, exposure to fire to examine secreted fluids (e.g. yielding amber-coloured coagulum), and use of the microscope for macerated preparations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description of uterine internal membrane, cotyledons, and placenta
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe mucous pelliculae attached to interior surface during pregnancy, tumors/appendices (cotyledons), their glandular structure, vascular connections to chorion, and appearance under maceration and injection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report texture (friable/loose or 'loose coherent'), color (ash-colour vs reddish parts), composition (vaginulae and sinuses), functional inference (gland forming nourishment for foetus), and microscopical appearance after maceration (radiculas forming 'forest' of capillaments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Observations on ovaria and corpora lutea
rubrics_metrics.description: Document vesicular bodies on ovaria (size, contents like coagulable albumen), formation and variability of the corpus luteum (size from vetch to cherry), vascularization and nervous supply, and presence of multiple corpora lutea without multiple fetuses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note whether vesiculae are true ova or pre-existing glandular matter; record whether corpora lutea are effete/pervious, internal cavity size, and effects of treatments (e.g. boiling) on appearance (vessels turgid with coagulated yellow juice). Use cross-species observations (cows, calves, women) to support inferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hypothesis on uterine contribution to fecundation
rubrics_metrics.description: Speculative criterion: uterine vessels and their contained viscid liquor may act as a semen-like fluid, contributing to fecundation in conjunction with semen masculinum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When proposing functional hypotheses, report observed features supporting them (vessels turgid in impregnation, viscid liquor qualities, continuity of vessels to cornua uteri), but mark as conjectural and indicate need for further evidence; describe how uterine liquor might mix with volatile particles of male semen to affect ovum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clock movement design: case and index construction
rubrics_metrics.description: Design details for a movement descended on an inclined plane: circular case of two plates and hoop, horary circle inscribed on forward plate, a central hemisphere (hollow upper half, lead-filled lower) with an index ornament or substitute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify dimensions (e.g. 3½ inches diameter for the case), construction (two plates fixed parallel by hoop, plates extend beyond hoop by 1/16 inch so movement can turn not slide), hemisphere mounted loosely on a hidden pin axis, lower part filled with lead to keep index pendulous pointing to vertical hour; ornament may be substituted by any index provided axis moves freely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clock movement mounting and stage requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for the stage or board on which the movement descends: straight, even surface about 6 feet long, thick enough not to warp or 'cast' with weather, raised at one end about 10° above horizon (angle variable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a non-warping board; raise stage end S about 10° (declivity DEH variable); ensure plates' edges are slightly indented so the movement turns rather than slides while descending; the stage length determines replacement frequency (6 feet stage requires resetting about once a week).

rubrics_metrics.name: Clock movement operation: measuring time by descent
rubrics_metrics.description: Operational principle: the movement placed near S moves down stage slowly to finish one entire revolution in 24 hours; hours shown by divisions on horary circle culminating successively under a fixed vertical index.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index should keep constant position (vertical hour), hour read by access of numbers to stationary index; after several revolutions when stage is consumed it must be replaced at S, which can be done quickly (less time than winding a watch); if stage is 6 feet, replacement frequency ~once a week.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clock adjustment and calibration
rubrics_metrics.description: Mechanisms and methods to adjust the rate and correct errors of the inclined-plane descent clock.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert a screw in the stage at S to elevate or depress the stage (raising speeds movement; lowering slows movement). Make the horary circle movable and provide small bosses or buttons on its verge so it may be shifted slightly left or right by finger to bring 'the just time' to the stationary index; use these adjustments to correct errors and calibrate to exact hours.
